card.name: Word right after a clause, before an outcome
card.fires_on: Short linking or verb words in general web text, such as "with", "killing", "pursued" or "make", that come right after a subject and lead into an outcome or action. Mostly nature, history and warning-style sentences.

modes.label: "with" after a state
modes.description: The word "with" follows a described condition and introduces a comparison or accompanying factor.
modes.example: The trees have been shredded as if<< with>> a saw.

modes.label: Harm or action verbs
modes.description: A verb about killing, pursuing or failing to survive, placed mid-sentence in a story about animals or battles.
modes.example: they strike the glass, often<< killing>> them.

modes.label: Words before a noun phrase
modes.description: A small word such as "a", "see" or "marked" sits right before the noun it modifies.
modes.example: Direct sunlight will kill the cuttings before they have<< a>> chance to root.

card.writes: It mildly promotes words about effort and running and suppresses Chinese words for suffering or experiencing, so the link to the output is weak.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in the middle of a sentence just before a result or action is named.
